sources.entry: PhotoPrism - Personal photo management powered by Go and Google TensorFlow. Browse, organize, and share your personal photo collection, using the latest technologies to automatically tag and find pictures. (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: PhotoPrism is a self-hosted, AI-assisted photo and video manager that lets you browse, search, tag, and share a personal media library.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes PhotoPrism as an AI-powered, privacy-first app for browsing, organizing, and sharing photos and videos, usable self-hosted or in the cloud. It automatically labels pictures by content and location and recognizes faces of family and friends. Search filters can be combined across properties such as labels, location, resolution, color, chroma, and quality. It reads metadata from Exif, XMP, and other sources like Google Photos, and handles RAW images and video formats for browsing. Access is through a PWA that can be installed on phones, tablets, and desktops, and WebDAV clients can connect to open, edit, and delete files. Some features (such as interactive world maps) are reserved for paying members.
use_cases: backing up phone photos from iOS or Android
browsing photos on a home server or Raspberry Pi
searching photos by location or labels
how_to_run: Install Docker, then follow the step-by-step instructions at docs.photoprism.app
Alternatively, use the tar.gz packages described in the Getting Started FAQ
notable: Automatic labeling and face recognition for pictures
Combinable search filters for labels, location, color, quality and more
Multi-arch Docker image supporting AMD, Intel, and ARM including Raspberry Pi and Apple Silicon
WebDAV access so desktop file managers can open and edit files directly
Privacy-focused: geocoding service designed to preserve privacy, no data sharing with big tech stated
caveats: Some features, such as interactive world maps, require a paid membership
Bug reports via GitHub Issues are discouraged unless fully reproducible; support goes through docs, discussions, and chat
Feature requests are not guaranteed to be implemented and release dates are not given
